candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest assigns MALWARE with probability 1.0000, and all 20 of the top n-grams push toward cryptojacking. The largest SHAP contributions come from instruction patterns typical of compute-heavy hashing and mixing code. The first is SIMD bitwise mixing: PXOR MOVAPS (+0.01449), PXOR MOVUPS (+0.00963), MOVDQA PAND (+0.00840), PAND PXOR (+0.00761) and PADDQ MOVDQA (+0.00590). The second is rotate/add/xor round structure: ADD ROR (+0.00962), ROL ADD (+0.00925), ADD ROL (+0.00549), ROL MOV (+0.00561) and SHRD XOR (+0.00732). The third is multi-precision or carry arithmetic: SUB ADC (+0.00548), SHL NEG (+0.00562) and SHL XCHG (+0.00585). MOVAPD DIVSD (+0.00614) indicates scalar floating-point division. The remaining n-grams (ADD PUSH, POP LEA, PUSH RET, CALL RET, CALL PUSH, POP PUSH) are generic call/stack-frame patterns. They contribute collectively (about +0.04) but are not specific to mining. The evidence supplies no function names, strings, or API information, so the verdict rests on instruction-level statistical signatures plus the model's unanimous output. Rotate/add/xor and SIMD mixing density is consistent with proof-of-work hashing loops, but the same patterns occur in legitimate cryptographic or compression libraries. That limits confidence below certainty.

evidence_analysis.assessment: Strongest single driver. SIMD XOR followed by an aligned 128-bit move is typical of vectorized state mixing or register clearing in hash/cipher inner loops. It is very rare in this binary (freq 0.000002) yet highly discriminative.
Generic arithmetic-to-stack transition. Probably reflects compiler-generated code around computation routines, so it is weak alone but adds to the malware signal.
Unaligned SIMD XOR/move variant, consistent with vectorized processing of data buffers such as hash state or scratchpad memory.
Add-then-rotate-right is a classic ARX (add-rotate-xor) primitive in hash functions and stream ciphers. It is relatively frequent (0.000118).
Rotate-left followed by add, another ARX round component. Together with ADD ROR and ADD ROL it suggests repeated round-based bit-diffusion code.
Aligned SIMD load followed by bitwise AND, consistent with masking and bit-selection in vectorized crypto or hashing routines.
Generic function-epilogue/address-computation pattern. Low specificity, but it contributes to the model's learned malware profile.
SIMD AND-then-XOR sequence, characteristic of boolean mixing functions in hash and cipher rounds.
Stack-manipulation/return pattern. Not intrinsically crypto-related, but it may point to unusual control flow or compact routines. Interpret cautiously.
Double-precision shift paired with XOR, used for wide-word shifts and diffusion in 64-bit-on-32-bit or multi-word hash arithmetic. It is a fairly specialized instruction.
Call immediately followed by return, indicating very small or thunk-like routines. Rare (freq 0.000001), and it contributes to the structural signature.
Common call-site pattern. Highest frequency among the top-20 (0.000425), but low specificity, so it acts as a supporting rather than decisive feature.
Register save/restore shuffling. A generic compiler idiom that adds mild support to the classification.

Double-precision floating-point move and divide. Very rare here (freq ~0), but it indicates numeric computation that the model associates with this malware class. Not a standard integer hashing indicator.
SIMD 64-bit lane addition followed by an aligned move, consistent with vectorized 64-bit arithmetic as used in many hash and PoW algorithms.
Shift followed by exchange. Very rare and unusual in typical code, and may reflect bit-manipulation or obfuscated arithmetic.
Shift-then-negate, a bit-twiddling idiom for mask generation or constant-time arithmetic, often seen in cryptographic implementations.
Rotate-left followed by a move, consistent with the rotate-based mixing seen in the other ARX n-grams.
Add-then-rotate-left, reinforcing the ARX round-function pattern. Frequent (0.000102), which suggests repeated use rather than incidental occurrence.
Subtract with carry propagation, indicating multi-word or big-integer arithmetic. It is a general crypto-math trait and not unique to mining.
